title: Shortest Path With At Most K Consecutive Identical Characters
summary: Given a directed weighted graph with n nodes, where each node has a label and a weight for each directed edge, find the minimum total edge weight of a path from node 0 to node n-1 with at most k consecutive identical characters in the path's label sequence.
statement: Given a directed weighted graph with n nodes, where each node has a label and a weight for each directed edge, find the minimum total edge weight of a path from node 0 to node n-1 with at most k consecutive identical characters in the path's label sequence. If no valid path exists, return -1.
constraints: Edges are directed and have positive weights.
The label sequence includes both endpoints and may contain at most k identical consecutive characters.
Return -1 when node n-1 is unreachable under that run constraint.
hints: The cheapest arrival at a node can still differ in how many repeated labels it carries.
Expand each graph node into states (node,current run length).
A different next label resets the run to one; an equal label increments it and is allowed only through k.
All weights are positive, so Dijkstra over the expanded states returns the first valid destination cost.
editorial: All weights are positive, so Dijkstra over the expanded states returns the first valid destination cost.

tests.explanation: The cheaper two-edge path begins with aa and is invalid, so the direct edge of cost three wins.
Allowing two equal labels makes the two-edge path valid with cost two.
